End-to-end monitoring is now available in the Cloud Pak: trace transactions across your runtimes
With the End-to-end monitoring instance type, you get visibility into transactions across multiple integration components. You can use it to trace requests, identify performance bottlenecks, and troubleshoot transaction failures.

For more information, see [Deploying end-to-end monitoring by using the CLI](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/install/deploy_e2e_monitoring.html "Use the CLI to deploy end-to-end monitoring, an instance type that monitors, traces, and analyzes transactions across multiple components including API Connect cluster, Event Gateway, Queue Manager, and App Connect runtime.") and [Using end-to-end monitoring](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/whats_next/using_e2e_monitoring.html). To get started with a tutorial, see [Tutorial: Setting up end-to-end transaction tracing across instances](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/tutorials/e2e_monitoring_tutorial.html "End-to-end monitoring gives you visibility into transactions across multiple integration components. You can use it to trace requests, identify performance bottlenecks, and troubleshoot transaction failures.").

Manage non-Kubernetes App Connect runtimes by using the Platform UI
By using a Platform UI and an App Connect dashboard, you can now configure the App Connect Private Networks feature that enables you to manage Non-Kubernetes App Connect runtimes from the Platform UI.

For more information, see [Configuring App Connect runtimes deployed in non-Kubernetes environments](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/whats_next/ace_remote_locations.html).

Reduced footprint and operational overhead for the Platform UI and Keycloak
Cloud Pak foundational services is no longer required for installing the Platform UI or any instance type that uses Keycloak for identity and access management. Cloud Pak foundational services is needed only for deploying the API Manager instance type. This change confers resource savings.

The update provides the following advantages:

*   Reduced operational overhead for managing operators, because the IBM Cloud Pak foundational services and the Operand Deployment Lifecycle Manager operators no longer need to be installed, upgraded, or managed.

*   Overall reduction of the footprint, by 1 CPU limit, when deploying the Platform UI (in other words, from 5.4 to 4.4 cores). This number includes all required operators and instances.

*   Faster install times when deploying the Platform UI, with a potential deployment time of under 5 minutes from instance creation.

*   Removal of the dependency on the EDB Postgres for Kubernetes operator and its catalog source pod. The Keycloak database is migrated from EDB Postgres for Kubernetes to IBM PostgreSQL, and it is now part of the IBM Cloud Pak for Integration operator.

Federated API management is now available in the Cloud Pak: extend the range of API runtimes locations you manage from a hub location
With the Federated API management instance type, you can connect, manage, and monitor multiple distributed API runtimes and data planes from a single interface. This instance type is supported by the API Connect operator.

For more information, see [Using Federated API management](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/whats_next/using_federated_api_management.html "Federated API Management provides a unified way to manage, govern, and monitor multiple distributed runtimes and data planes from a single interface regardless of where they are deployed.").

Managing API Nano Gateways in the Platform UI
The API Nano Gateway provides a Cloud-native gateway that uses a componentized architecture with a small footprint. You can now create, view, and manage these instances in the Platform UI.

For more information, see [Using the DataPower Nano Gateway to secure an application domain](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/api-connect/software/12.1.1?topic=cli-using-datapower-nano-gateway-secure-application-domain "(Opens in a new tab or window)").

Managing API Developer Portals in the Platform UI
API Developer Portals enable organizations to securely expose APIs to external developers, partners, and other consumers to use in building their own applications on their platforms.

You can now create, view, and manage these instances in the Platform UI. If a specific API Developer Portal instance has an API Analytics instance associated with it, the API Analytics instance is nested below it in the list of created instances.

For more information about API Developer Portals, see [Overview](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/api-connect/software/12.1.0?topic=portal-overview "(Opens in a new tab or window)") in the IBM API Connect documentation.

Direct linkage to license usage reporting and analytics
In the Platform UI, a **Usage analytics** option is now available in the **Administration** section of the navigation panel. When clicked, it provides access to license usage reporting and analytics. By default, the link directs users to IBM Software Central.

If a License Service Reporter is installed in your cluster, the link automatically points to the reporter's URL. Administrators can also configure a custom URL by setting an environment variable.

For more information about License Service Reporter, see [License Service Reporter](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/cloud-paks/foundational-services/4.19.x?topic=license-service-reporter "(Opens in a new tab or window)") in the Cloud Pak foundational services documentation.

Stop and restart instances by using the Platform UI
You can now stop and restart instances by clicking a **Stop** (or **Start**) button in the instances table of the Platform UI. Instances that support this functionality are App Connect runtimes, Queue managers, Enterprise gateways, and Messaging servers.

For more information, see "Stopping and restarting instances" in [Using the Platform UI](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/whats_next/using_platform_ui.html).

Improved filtering options in the Platform UI
The Platform UI now allows users to easily share filtered views. When users filter the instances table, your browser's URL is updated. adding parameters that reflect those filters. The updated URL can be shared with other users so they can access the same filter.

For example, when the instances table is filtered for Queue managers, the `/instances` URL changes to `/instances?filters=type%3AQueue%2520manager`.

Expanded layout for instance creation and edit
The create and edit experiences in the Platform UI now use a full-page layout. The new format allows the UI form or YAML to expand across the screen, for improved usability on wider displays.

The assembly canvas also supports this expanded layout, providing more space for building and configuring integrations. When clicked, nodes on the canvas open in full-page format for a better editing experience in the UI form or YAML.

Cloud Pak for Integration Agent
The IBM Cloud Pak for Integration Agent, available in the Platform UI, enables a conversational interface that is powered by LLMs. Users can ask the interface to perform health checks, return the status of instances, troubleshoot problems, and find out if there are updates. This agent replaces the Cloud Pak for Integration Agent Preview.

For more information, see [Using the Cloud Pak for Integration Agent](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/whats_next/using_platform_ui_add_on.html).

Downloading the instances table as a CSV
You can download a comma-separated values (CSV) file that contains a complete list of deployed instances.

For more information, see "Downloading the instances table as a CSV" in [Using the Platform UI](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/whats_next/using_platform_ui.html).

Enhanced instance navigation in the Platform UI
The Platform UI now provides direct access to instances from the navigation panel. Users can navigate to instances grouped by type (App Connect dashboard, App Connect designer, API Manager, Event Manager, Event Processing, Kafka cluster, and Queue manager) by clicking the main menu icon. Instance types are displayed alphabetically with corresponding icons.

Queue Manager behaves slightly differently; the entries in the navigation panel navigate to a page that displays all filtered Queue Manager instances.

Multi-replica support for instance locations
You can run the hub Platform UI with multiple replicas when using instance locations. This configuration supports highly available hub deployments while continuing to display instances from all connected locations.

For more information, see [Managing instances across multiple locations](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/SSGT7J_16.2.0/whats_next/instance_locations_about.html).

Enhancement to the upgrade plan
When upgrading to 16.2.0 by using the upgrade plan, users get a new step that detects deployed integration server instances and flags them as removed. Users get instructions on how to convert the integration servers to App Connect runtimes.

For more information, see [App Connect Integration Server reference](https://www.ibm.com/links?url=https%3A%2F%2Fibm.biz%2Faceintsrvrop-v13 "(Opens in a new tab or window)").

Visual preview for Assembly assets within Automation Assets
Integration Assembly assets within Automation Assets now provide a canvas preview, in addition to the existing code preview. When you browse or click to open an Assembly asset, the canvas view renders the integration visually, making it easier to understand the asset at a glance and select the right asset. (4.4.2)
